value.account: Working tree already contained a prior attempt's edits (validation.py reorder, executor.py ref-follow, new tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_paths_e2e.py); I reviewed and kept them. Changes: (1) orchestrator/workflow/validation.py _validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted: the exact compiler-emitted generated loop-frame ref check now runs before the relpath 'may only override scalar' rejection, so only that exact ref (tracked per step/output) is allowed on relpath outputs; authored literals/other refs for relpath outputs are still rejected. (2) orchestrator/workflow/executor.py structured-output resolution: when a resolved value is exactly {'ref': str} (an on_exhausted override stored as a loop-frame ref), follow it once; without this, validation passed but exhaustion failed at runtime (verified by reverting: 2.29/2.32 exhaustion tests fail). (3) Tests: 2.28/2.29/2.32 exhaustion, approval path output, and malformed provider path still failing. Tried and discarded: widening _capture_generated_repeat_until_on_exhausted_refs to nested steps via _iter_authored_step_mappings — not needed, reverted. Considered resolving refs in loops.repeat_until_exhaustion_artifacts, but it lacks state/scope access. Ran loop/recur, loop-state, rich-loop, exhaustion-state, imported-stdlib exhaustion, and new e2e modules (99 passed) plus loader_validation exhaust selector. Not covered: no full suite; the executor ref-follow is generic to any single-key {'ref'} dict value in structured outputs (object-typed outputs with exactly that shape would be dereferenced); 2.28 and earlier code paths untouched; the e2e test reads the source from bugs/ rather than copying it.
value.summary: Fixed 2.29+ rejection/failure of loop results with path fields in non-exhausted union variants by accepting compiler-generated exhaustion placeholder refs for relpath outputs in validation and resolving those refs at runtime.

value.account: Dos causas. (1) orchestrator/workflow/validation.py, _validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted: el rechazo 'may only override scalar' de salidas relpath se evaluaba antes de comprobar el ref generado por el compilador (placeholder de variante inactiva, emitido solo desde 2.29); ahora se comprueba primero el ref generado exacto, de modo que un override authored sobre relpath sigue rechazado (test existente en test_loader_validation.py). (2) orchestrator/workflow/loops.py, repeat_until_exhaustion_artifacts: en agotamiento los overrides {ref:...} se guardaban como payload sin resolver; el join de match estructurado (2.29+) los valida como valor y fallaba con invalid_relpath/invalid_integer. Ahora, solo si la version del workflow es >=2.29, los overrides ref-only se resuelven a su valor (artefacto propio del bucle o _resolve_ref_value); 2.28 y anteriores no cambian. Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_paths.py (programa del bug en 2.28/2.29/2.32, rutas exhausted/done/escalated, con proveedor simulado); antes del arreglo fallaban exhausted-2.29/2.32. Modulos ejecutados: ese, test_workflow_loops_exhaustion_state, test_workflow_lisp_loop_recur, test_workflow_lisp_rich_loop_values_e2e, test_workflow_executor_characterization, test_loader_validation (333 pasan). Alternativas descartadas: resolver solo overrides de salidas relpath (dejaba fallar la salida entera 'rounds'); resolver en _resolve_bound_address para cualquier artefacto ref-only (podria reinterpretar datos legitimos con forma {ref}); relajar el validador para cualquier relpath (debilita la validacion). No cubierto: no se ejecuto la suite completa; el test de salida de proveedor mal formado depende de los tests existentes; resume tras agotamiento en 2.29+ no probado explicitamente.
value.summary: El bucle loop/recur con campo path en una variante no agotada ahora compila y se ejecuta (incluido el agotamiento) en 2.29-2.32 igual que en 2.28.

value.account: Two defects. (1) orchestrator/workflow/validation.py _validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted rejected any on_exhausted override of a relpath output before checking whether the value was the compiler-emitted generated ref (the 2.29+ lowering emits an exhausted-placeholder ref for inactive-variant path fields). I moved the generated-ref check ahead of the relpath rejection; that check is only enabled for compiler-generated workflows and requires the exact captured ref, so authored relpath overrides are still rejected. (2) Once it compiled, exhaustion failed at runtime: at 2.29+ the UNRESOLVED case reads result__rounds from the loop frame, which held the raw {'ref': ...} dict (2.28 read state__round directly). orchestrator/workflow/loops.py repeat_until_exhaustion_artifacts now substitutes root.steps.<step>.artifacts.<name> refs with the loop's frame artifact or the named step's committed artifact, gated to workflow version >=2.29 so <=2.28 persisted state is unchanged (an existing test pins the raw ref at older targets). Unresolvable refs are left as-is. Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_union_paths.py runs a union loop through run_workflow at 2.28/2.29/2.32 for exhaustion and approval, plus malformed provider path (../escape.md) still fails. Ran that module plus loop_recur, rich_loop_values_e2e, loader_validation, wcc_m4/m5, scoped_union_guards, verified_iteration_drain, imported_stdlib exhaustion: 406 passed. Considered and discarded: making the validator accept relpath overrides generally (weakens validation); changing the lowering to read state fields directly like 2.28 (would alter 2.29+ lowering/fingerprints for all programs). Not covered: nested/imported loops whose on_exhausted refs use non-root step names fall back to the raw ref; resume of a run interrupted mid-exhaustion was not exercised; full suite not run per instructions. No explicit new loader test for authored relpath rejection (existing loader_validation tests cover it and pass).
value.summary: Loop results with path fields outside the exhausted variant now compile and run at 2.29-2.32 like 2.28, via a validator reorder plus runtime resolution of compiler-emitted exhaustion refs.

value.account: Two root causes. (1) orchestrator/workflow/validation.py _validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted rejected any relpath-typed output before checking for the compiler-emitted generated ref; since 2.29 lowering emits a placeholder ref (…__exhausted_placeholders) for the inactive variant's path field. I moved the generated-ref check ahead of the relpath rejection; the check only passes for the exact ref the compiler captured for that step/output (and only when the lowering opts in), so authored relpath overrides, literals and wrong refs are still rejected (tests/test_loader_validation.py passes). (2) With that fixed, the 2.32 run still failed on exhaustion, even for a union with no path fields: orchestrator/workflow/loops.py left {ref} override dicts in the loop frame artifacts and the 2.29+ lowering reads result__rounds via the loop artifact, so the structured match output validation saw a dict. Added _resolve_exhaustion_refs, applied to exhausted artifacts only when workflow version >= 2.29 (frame refs resolved from the exhaustion frame snapshot, others via executor._resolve_ref_value; unresolved raises LoopStateIntegrityError). 2.28 and earlier take the unchanged path. Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_path_variants.py runs a reduced version of the bug program end to end (mocked providers) at 2.28/2.29/2.32 for exhaustion and the approve path, and checks a nonexistent provider-reported path still fails the run; also ran the bug's dry-run at 2.32 successfully and the loop/exhaustion/rich-loop/loader-validation modules (305 passed). Considered: changing lowering to emit state refs as in 2.28 (rejected: the placeholder is needed for rich values at 2.29+ and the relpath still hits the validator); loosening the validator for all relpath overrides (rejected: weakens validation). Not covered: resume mid-exhaustion, the full suite (not run per instructions), and loops whose exhaustion refs point into non-frame steps beyond the placeholder step. I did not edit bugs/. Note: repo CLAUDE.md asks for Spanish replies to the user; this report stays in English for the machine-read bundle.
value.summary: At targets 2.29+ a loop/recur union result whose non-exhausted variant has a path field now compiles and runs like 2.28: the validator accepts the compiler-generated exhaustion placeholder ref for relpath outputs, and the runtime resolves exhaustion ref overrides to values.
